verdict.rationale: Gmail's own delegation feature lets one or more people read, send and delete mail in a single account, which gives a team shared access to one mailbox. Nothing in the evidence describes team channels, collaborative inbox views, assignment, or how shared read and conversation state stays consistent across team members. missing for 10: documented shared or collaborative inbox or team-channel feature, explicit shared conversation state (read status, assignment, ownership) across members, independent hands-on corroboration of team use.

support.subject: As a team-lead, my team works shared inboxes together — shared accounts or team channels where everyone sees the same conversation state

citations.quote: You can grant one or more delegates access to your Gmail account. A delegate is someone who can read, send, and delete emails in your account for you.
Delegates can read, send, and delete messages, as well as view and add contacts on behalf of the delegator's account.
